name: numerical: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time…

request.questionText: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time that we analyzed in class and in Lesson 14. Specifically, we'll consider three variables from this data set (two that we looked at before, and one that we didn't): PictureTarget.RT: the subject's reaction time in milliseconds when presented with a visual stimulus FarAway: a dummy variable for whether the stimulus (i.e. the “bad guy” popping up on the screen) was near (0) or far away (1) within the visual scene. SceneLetter: a letter code (b, c, d, e, or f) indicating which of five scenes the subject was presented with. (Note: the scene letters start at b; there is no scene a in this data set) Consider the following model and its corresponding regression table: lm(PictureTarget.RT ~ FarAway + SceneLetter + FarAway:SceneLetter, data=rxntime) %>% get_regression_table() %>% select(-std_error, - statistic, - p_value) Based on this regression table, what is the predicted reaction time for Scene b when the stimulus is not far away? Enter your answer rounded to the nearest millisecond.
